title: MOD ( -3, 2 ) is 1 and MOD ( 3, -2 ) is -1: the sign follows the divisor

source.quote: The result always has the same sign as the divisor.

source.supports: the definition in terms of INT

derivation: MOD ( -3, 2 ) = -3 - 2 * INT ( -1.5 ) = -3 - 2 * -2 = 1. MOD ( 3, -2 ) = 3 - ( -2 ) * INT ( -1.5 ) = 3 - 4 = -1. A remainder that truncates (as in C) would give -1 and 1.
notes: The type is not asserted (see mod-positive).
